answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each identity to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where minting replica identities incurs superlinear cost scaling as $C(k) \propto k^{2.5}$. An attacker attempting to mirror multiple agents generates a traceable zero-knowledge plume that penalizes concurrent claims. Retiring old identities leaves a non-transferable relic token required to access high-tier consensus pools, forcing exponential financial friction on attackers.
